labrador.paper: Beullens, Seiler. LaBRADOR: Compact Proofs for R1CS from Module-SIS. CRYPTO 2023; ePrint 2022/1341
labrador.statement: dot-product constraints over R_q (ring-scalar x full inner products + linear terms) with one global l2 norm bound; R1CS mod 2^64+1 by reduction (Section 6)
labrador.assumption: MSIS over R_q = Z_q[X]/(X^64+1), q ~ 2^32 single precision (high inertia degree required: not NTT-friendly)
labrador.prover: O(N) ring multiplications plus r x N aggregation products (h_ij = <phi_i, s_j>), multi-modular NTT (Greyhound library)
labrador.knowledge_error: 2^-125 per recursion level (Theorem 5.1), slack sqrt(128/30) ~ 2 on the extracted norm; ~7 levels for 50 KB
labrador.zk: not in the paper; LNP22 shim in the LaZer toolkit (Biasioli et al. 2026/1289)
labrador.implementation: lattice-dogs/labrador (C, AVX-512, single-thread; also Greyhound); LaZer; icicle-labrador (GPU, broken ring per zkSecurity 2026-04-30)

greyhound.paper: Nguyen, Seiler. Greyhound: Fast Polynomial Commitments from Lattices. CRYPTO 2024; ePrint 2024/1293
greyhound.statement: univariate polynomial evaluation (sqrt(N) x sqrt(N) reshape, three-round core) composed with LaBRADOR
greyhound.assumption: MSIS, d = 64, q ~ 2^32 multi-precision (q = 5 mod 8), challenges tau_1 = 32 (Section 5)

prover_seconds_measured.hardware: one Intel Xeon Sapphire Rapids core at 3.2 GHz, AVX-512 (Table 2)

greyhound.zk: sketched (LWE randomness on outer commitments, L=4 masks; +0.75 KB)

hachi.paper: Nguyen, O'Rourke, Zhang. Hachi: Efficient Lattice-Based Multilinear Polynomial Commitments over Extension Fields. ePrint 2026/156
hachi.statement: multilinear evaluation over F_{q^k} reduced to R_q statements; sumcheck over an extension field via ring switching (verifier does no R_q multiplication)
hachi.assumption: MSIS (l_inf), q ~ 2^32, d = 2^10 (5.2), 128-bit via the Lattice Estimator

akita.paper: Dao, Bodaghi, Khajehpour, Vitto, Badakhshan, Georghiades, Liu, Zhang, Thaler. Akita: A High-Performance Lattice-Based PCS. ePrint 2026/1983
akita.statement: multilinear PCS (K-ary fold to completion, setup offloading), batched openings, pay-per-bit commitment; integrated in Jolt (non-ZK)
akita.assumption: MSIS at per-matrix ring dimensions (64 / 32 / 16 ...), moduli 2^32-99, 64-bit, 128-bit profiles (Table 5); exact Euclidean norm checks
akita.digit_range_check: balanced base-b digits, w -> w(w+1) symmetry, GKR-style product tree: O(bL) prover (6.1)
akita.zk: none ('akita and zk cannot be enabled together' in Jolt; listed as future work)
akita.implementation: Rust (a16z/jolt crates/jolt-akita); GPU/Metal for Jolt, PCS kernels unstated

latticefold_plus.statement: folding of CCS/R1CS instances over a 64-bit field; algebraic (monomial) range proof; double commitments
latticefold_plus.prover: 5-10x faster than LatticeFold (paper estimate); no public benchmark of a full prover found

neo_superneo.paper: Nethermind (Setty et al.). Neo and SuperNeo: post-quantum folding with pay-per-bit costs over small fields. ePrint 2026/242 (Neo 2025/294)
neo_superneo.statement: CCS over an extension field of a small prime, HyperNova-style single sumcheck, Ajtai commitments with pay-per-bit cost, multi-folding
neo_superneo.note: Ajtai hash quoted 30x faster than Pedersen (Boneh's ZKProof7 slides citing Nethermind)

symphony.paper: Chen. Symphony: Scalable SNARKs in the ROM from lattice-based high-arity folding. ePrint 2025/1905
symphony.statement: high-arity folding of NP statements, degree-3 sumcheck over an extension field; prover dominated by committing the input witnesses

lova.paper: Fenzi, Knabenhans, Nguyen, Pham. Lova: lattice folding from unstructured lattices. ePrint 2024/1964
lova.statement: Nova-style folding with an unstructured SIS commitment, power-of-two moduli, exact Euclidean norm proof
lova.note: unstructured A: the commitment is a plain dense Z_{2^k} matmul (ideal tensor-core shape) at the price of a lambda x larger matrix

hyperwolf.paper: Zhang, Gao, Xiao. HyperWolf / HyperWolf*: lattice PCS with O(log N) proof and verifier. ePrint 2025/922 (Oct 2025 revision)
hyperwolf.statement: k-dimensional tensor folding of the witness; exact Euclidean norm via <f,f> mod q = <f,f> over Z

rok_family.paper: Klooss, Lai, Nguyen, Osadnik et al.: RoK Paper SISsors (2025), RoK and Roll (2025), SALSAA (2025), RoKoKo (2025)
rok_family.statement: verifier-succinct reductions of knowledge with exact norm bounds; RoKoKo measured in Akita Table 8 (8.27 s commit / 4.43 s open at 2^35 bits, 109-115 KB, 100-bit statistical soundness)
rok_family.assumption: vanishing-SIS or related structured assumptions for the polylog-verifier results (not plain MSIS)

zksecurity_labrador_bugs.source: Raikos, Wong. Soundness failures in LaBRADOR implementations from NTT-friendly rings. zkSecurity, 2026-04-30
zksecurity_labrador_bugs.finding: icicle-labrador (GPU, composite BabyBear x KoalaBear q, fully splitting ring) ~31 bits of soundness; condor-rs ~6; Lazarus ~1; lattice-dogs and LaZer unaffected
zksecurity_labrador_bugs.consequence: the NTT-friendly-ring GPU shortcut is not available to LaBRADOR-style aggregation; sumcheck-based systems aggregate over E instead

q64_chunk16.name: q64_chunk16
q64_chunk16.basis: exact embedding needs q > 2^~52 (exact_embedding); Akita p64 profile; the source is committed in the checker's own 16-bit range chunks (no source digit range check: the checker's lookups bound them, binding holds for weak openings), collision bound 2^16

q64_hex.name: q64_hex
q64_hex.basis: as q64_chunk16 but the source is re-decomposed into balanced base-16 digits (Hachi/Akita alphabet): 4x the digits, smaller MSIS output

q32_chunk16.name: q32_chunk16
q32_chunk16.basis: LaBRADOR/Greyhound/Akita p32 modulus; the checker needs the small-field repairs (F1) and a q = 5 mod 8 prime (not BabyBear); priced on tensor.py's BabyBear^6 A row

exact_embedding.why: a lattice norm bound is global (one l2 or l_inf bound, extracted with slack ~2 by JL or exact by <f,f> lifting) and certifies binding; the checker's 27k per-value range predicates per VU are exact per-coordinate statements and stay constraints (digit vanishing polynomials or the lookup argument).  Nothing in the checker is cheaper because the witness is short, except the commitment itself (pay-per-bit).

ajtai_commit_A_q64_chunk16.shape: (896) x (44202) x B, INT8 dense GEMM
ajtai_commit_A_q64_chunk16.note: NTT-domain evaluation would turn the short digits into full Z_q elements (lq x lq per product): the coefficient-domain GEMM keeps pay-per-bit

rows.proof_kb_per_batch_opening: 61-72 (Akita Table 8) per opening; plus the checker sumcheck transcript
caveats: the sumcheck field must contain Z_q: with q = 64-bit the checker sumcheck runs on 8-limb elements (priced on tensor.py's A/Goldilocks^3 row); with q = 32-bit the prime must be q = 5 mod 8 (LS18 invertible short challenges) or use RoKoKo-style probabilistic invertibility: BabyBear (fully splitting) is not the LaBRADOR/Greyhound choice; the small-field repairs (F1/F3/F4) are re-derived for the new prime (priced on the BabyBear^6 row)

no range check on the source digits: they are the checker's own 16-bit range chunks (bounded by its lookups) and binding holds for weak openings; the exact range check acts on the folded response (Akita 6.1).  A one-shot PCS needs no norm proof on the source; a recursive/IVC use (LatticeFold) would

knowledge error: LaBRADOR Theorem 5.1 gives 2^-125 per level at d = 64 (challenge set > 2^128 before operator-norm rejection); Akita reaches its 128-bit budget with per-fold accounting; a 2^-128 batch bound over the union of folds, range layers and the checker sumcheck is NOT established here: 2^-120 .. 2^-125 is what the papers deliver at d = 64

ZK: Akita has none; Greyhound sketches LWE-randomised outer commitments; LaBRADOR needs the LaZer LNP22 shim (linear size). Malicious-verifier ZK adds MLWE to the assumption set and is unbuilt in every implementation found
utilisation 0.172 applied to the fold and range sumchecks (dense, as TensorZKP's); the Ajtai GEMM would run far above it

greyhound_cpu_anchor.basis: Greyhound Table 2, N = 2^30 coefficients, commit + prove on one Sapphire Rapids core; a PCS opening, not a constraint proof

notes: the r x N term is the base protocol's amortisation cost; recursion levels are smaller and not priced
one wire per ring element wastes d - 1 coefficients of every commitment and NTT; packing d wires per element breaks coordinate-wise products
not a candidate: the sumcheck-based route (design_lattice_pcs) is the only lattice construction that fits the checker's constraint shape

best.soundness_reached: 2^-120 .. 2^-125 at d = 64 (LaBRADOR Thm 5.1 per level; Akita per-fold budget) -- not 2^-128 without a larger ring or repetition

verdict.complete_alternative_backend: NO. Every lattice system that fits the checker's coordinate-wise quadratic constraints is 'a sumcheck over an extension field + an Ajtai-committed witness' (Hachi/Akita/Neo/Symphony/LatticeFold+); its prover is A's prover with the commitment layer swapped, so it cannot beat A by more than A's encoding + hashing buckets (20% of A at 50 GB/s) minus its own fold and digit range check.  The LaBRADOR dot-product route is 100x+ worse at one wire per ring element.  C (3.1e6, designated verifier) is untouched.
verdict.reusable_component: MAYBE, conditional: a lattice PCS (Ajtai GEMM on the checker's own 16-bit chunks + Akita-style K-ary fold + exact digit range check on the response) replacing RS-Ligero + Merkle in A is hash-free; its commitment is the best-shaped INT8 GEMM in the design space (kappa d x digits x 4096, 6.3e8 limb MACs/VU at the Akita-anchored kappa d = 896) and the model puts A+lattice-PCS at 1.01x A (32-bit q, BabyBear row, 1.08e7) to 0.74x A (64-bit q, Goldilocks^3 row, 9.3e6 vs 1.25e7) at 50 GB/s Blake3 and fold arity 64 -- inside the hash-rate uncertainty (A at 10 GB/s is 2.5e7: the swap wins 2.7x; at 190 GB/s A is ~9.5e6: the swap loses) and inside the fold-arity sensitivity (K = 16: 1.46e7, K = 256: 9.6e6).  Costs: +~20 sequential rounds, MSIS (+MLWE for hiding) added to the assumption set, no ZK in any implementation, knowledge error ~2^-120..-125 at d = 64, a 64-bit q for exactness or a q = 5 mod 8 32-bit prime with the small-field repairs redone.  For B it is not a component: B loses its row tests and becomes an explicit-trace Spartan design (the 7.9e6 of that row is the flattening of A's layered GKR, obtainable with Ligero too, not a lattice effect).
verdict.follow_up_first_build: Nothing before the GPU Blake3/Poseidon2 hash rate is measured (tensor.md uncertainty 2): the whole case for the swap is the hash bucket.  If it lands below ~30 GB/s: (1) run jolt-akita (Rust, 32-bit profile) on A's committed object (44k 16-bit chunks/VU x 4096) on vy-cpu2 for a measured commit+open per VU beside the Ligero CPU number; (2) write the INT8 Ajtai GEMM kernel (A shared across the batch) and measure its utilisation on the L40S; (3) price the response range check against logUp on the same digits with a real fold schedule (Akita's planner).  No lattice lane before that.

uncertainties.what: digit range check + fold opening as tensor-core sumchecks (priced as degree-3 / degree-2 sumchecks over 2x / 1x the digits at 0.172 utilisation)
uncertainties.moves: the lattice additions (~40% of the PCS-swap delta); Akita's O(bL) SIMT count and small-value tricks may be cheaper, a proper accounting of all folds costlier

uncertainties.what: Merkle hash rate on SIMT in the reference (what the lattice PCS removes)
uncertainties.moves: the saving: at 10 GB/s A/Goldilocks is 2.5e7 and the swap wins 2.7x; at 190 GB/s A's hash bucket is 0.03 s per batch and the swap loses

uncertainties.what: MSIS output size and modulus (heuristic kappa d; q = 64-bit for exactness vs 32-bit with small-field repairs; d = 64 vs larger rings for the challenge set)
uncertainties.range: 0.3x - 3x on the Ajtai GEMM (the raw BKZ model under-shoots the Akita anchor 3.6x and is scaled to it); +17% on the checker sumcheck if the field must be 64-bit
uncertainties.moves: commitment MACs (7% of the row at kappa d = 896) and whether the checker sumcheck stays on 4-limb elements

assumptions: Every figure is an ESTIMATE from this module's docstrings over the WP2 checker census; the only measured numbers are the cited papers' CPU benchmarks (Greyhound Table 2, Akita Tables 8-9) and tensor.py's TensorZKP calibration (utilisation 0.172).
Widths not in the census: looked-up columns 16 bits, query wires 32 bits, products/materialised 32 bits (LOOKUP_OUTPUT_BITS, QUERY_WIRE_BITS, PRODUCT_BITS).

MSIS output size from the heuristic in msis_output_bits (BKZ root-Hermite 1.005, column-restriction attack), rounded up to a multiple of d; the Lattice Estimator replaces it.  Scaled (ANCHOR_SCALE = 3.57) to reproduce Akita Table 5: rank-1 d=64 q=2^32 binary map = 2048 output bits at 147 quantum bits.
Ajtai commitment as a coefficient-domain INT8 GEMM (A entries ceil(q_bits/8) limbs, digits 1 limb); response commitment at 2x the input commitment.

Fold opening = one degree-2 sumcheck over the digits (first-fold dominated); digit range check = degree-3 sumcheck over 2x the digits (product tree); both at 0.172 of the H100 INT8 peak; Hadamards on SIMT at tensor.py's rates; hint generation as tensor.py.
The non-commitment buckets (GKR checker, logUp fractional GKR, Hadamards) are tensor.py's Candidate A BabyBear^6 row unchanged; the field caveat is stated per row.
LaBRADOR-direct: r = N^(1/3), one wire per ring element, ring product d^2 scalar MACs (no NTT: q must not split), base protocol only.
